Let me analyze what happened after clicking the purple square's magenta center (28,36):
Before:
- W at ring center (21,39) - 12 pixels
- Purple square at (28,36) - 20 pixels
- G at (35,34) - 12 pixels
After:
- W at (26-29, 34-38) - 9 pixels (moved down from ring)
- Purple square at (28-33, 33-37) - 21 pixels (moved down slightly)
- G at (34-37, 32-36) - 11 pixels (moved down slightly)
The white diamond moved from the ring center (21,39) to the purple square's position, but it didn't swap cleanly. Instead, the white diamond is now at (26-29, 34-38) which is between the ring and the purple square. The purple square moved down to (28-33, 33-37) and the dark gray diamond moved down to (34-37, 32-36).
The objects are all getting closer together again, and the white diamond shrank from 12 to 9 pixels.
This is similar to what happened in click 5 and 7. When the white diamond is at the ring and I click an object below, the white diamond moves toward that object and the objects compress.
Let me think about the pattern:
1. When W is at the ring and I click an object below, W moves toward it and objects compress.
2. When W is NOT at the ring and I click an object below, W swaps with that object.
3. When objects are compressed and I click the ring, they spread out and W goes to the ring.
So the mechanic seems to be:
- Clicking the ring center: W goes to ring, objects spread out.
- Clicking an object when W is at ring: W moves toward clicked object, objects compress.
- Clicking an object when W is NOT at ring: W swaps with clicked object.
The goal might be to get all three objects to merge into one at the ring position. Or maybe the goal is to get the white diamond to "collect" all the other objects.
Let me try clicking the dark gray diamond's purple center at (35,34) to see if W moves there and compresses the chain further.
